gm.title: Description
lines: The marikith hunters of Timor live in dark tunnels around a queen. They frighten their prey before closing in.

gm.title: Running the encounter
lines: Use small packs outside the hive. In the hive, send two or three hunters first and increase the size of each wave until the hunters outnumber their opponents at least ten to one. The queen remains inside and issues telepathic orders to her brood within 5 miles. Her printed encounter lists an escort of 4–48 hunters.

gm.title: Light sensitivity
lines: All marikith take −1 on attack rolls in candlelight or starlight, −2 in torchlight, and −4 in bright sunlight or within daylight.

gm.title: Hunter tactics
lines: Hunters squeeze through gaps and use mimicry to isolate their prey. To fool a listener, a hunter opposes the listener's Listen check with Bluff and gains a +8 racial bonus on the roll. The queen's bulk prevents her from using the hunters' Compression ability.

gm.title: Transformation
lines: The book presents a failed powers check in Timor as a rumored route to transformation, taking 1d6 hours. The queen's sting provides a separate confirmed encounter mechanic. A humanoid paralyzed by the sting changes into a hunter within a week. Neutralizing the poison before completion reverses the change.

gm.title: Description
lines: A rubbery black hunter slips through drains and barred openings. Packs lure prey with copies of their voices.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any underground environment in Timor. Pairs, packs of 2–8 or swarms of 2–20. Always lawful evil. No treasure or level adjustment. Advancement 4–5 HD (Medium).

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +8. AC +4 Dex, +3 natural. Touch 14, flat-footed 13. Base attack +2, printed grapple +3. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +2, Ref +5, Will +5.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Escape Artist +16, Hide +12, Listen +6, Move Silently +12, Spot +4. Improved Initiative. Racial bonuses: +8 Escape Artist, +4 Hide and Move Silently.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Darkvision 120 ft. Takes half damage from bludgeoning weapons and is immune to fear, horror and madness. Hunters are under the influence of their queen.
Light Sensitivity (Ex). Attack rolls take −1 in candlelight or starlight, −2 in torchlight, and −4 in bright sunlight or within a daylight spell.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +5 melee for 1d4 + 3.
Full attack. Two claws +5 melee for 1d4 + 3 each and bite +0 melee for 2d4 + 3.
Compression (Ex). While moving, pass through a gap at least 1 ft. across as a free action. A gap 7–11 inches across takes a move action. A gap 3–6 inches across takes a full-round action. Smaller gaps are impassable.
Voice Mimicry (Ex). The hunter has no true language but can imitate voices and sounds. Resolve deception with its Bluff check at a +8 racial bonus opposed by the listener’s Listen check.

gm.title: Running the encounter
lines: Hunters torment prey before striking. Outside the hive they hunt in small packs. In the hive the first wave has two or three hunters, and each later wave grows until the intruders are outnumbered at least ten to one.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The single-attack line omits claw damage, so use the matching claw damage in Full Attack. The printed grapple modifier is +3 even though the printed base attack and Strength yield +5 under the usual calculation.

gm.title: Description
lines: This spiderlike queen breeds the hunters of Timor. She stays inside the hive and directs her brood against intruders.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +1. AC components −2 size, +1 Dex, +10 natural. Touch AC 9, flat-footed AC 18. Base attack +7, grapple +15. Space 10 ft., reach 10 ft. Fort +8, Ref +4, Will +9.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +15 melee (2d4 + 8).
Full attack. Four claws +15 melee (2d4 + 8 each), plus either bite +10 melee (2d8 + 4 and poison) or sting +10 melee (1d8 + 4 and poison).
Improved Grab (Ex). After at least two claws hit a Medium or smaller target, attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity.
Poison (Ex). Bite and sting both require DC 20 Fortitude saves. For the bite, use 2d6 initial Constitution damage and 1d6 secondary Constitution damage. The sting has no initial damage and causes one week of secondary paralysis. An affected humanoid becomes a marikith hunter during that week. Neutralizing the poison before the change finishes reverses the transformation.

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 5/piercing. Darkvision 120 ft. Immune to fear, horror, and madness. Hive Mind (Su) lets her communicate telepathically with any of her brood within 5 miles. Light Sensitivity (Ex) imposes a −1 attack penalty in candlelight or starlight, −2 in torchlight, and −4 in bright sunlight or daylight. The block also lists Voice Mimicry.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Balance +9, Hide +5, Listen +10, Move Silently +7, Search +3, Spot +8. Improved Grab, Multiattack.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Underground in Timor. A queen is escorted by 4–48 hunters. Always neutral evil. Double standard treasure. Advancement 11–16 HD (Huge).

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The bite description repeats “secondary damage” with two different values. For play, use 2d6 initial and the explicitly repeated 1d6 secondary. The queen has Voice Mimicry in her stat line, but only the hunter entry gives a procedure. As a table default, use opposed Bluff with a +8 racial bonus against Listen, as for the hunters.
The queen’s printed stat line gives a 10-ft. space and +15 grapple. The full-attack line omits bite poison, which is specified in the combat description on p. 150.

lines: The Fury called the Disputatious brings arcane magic to the trio’s hunt.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any land or underground. Triune with her sisters. Always lawful evil. No treasure or level adjustment. Advances as a sorcerer.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +3. AC +3 Dex, +2 natural. Touch 13, flat-footed 12. Printed base attack +3 and grapple +3. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +8, Ref +9, Will +9.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +18, Concentration +15, Diplomacy +19, Gather Information +17, Intimidate +15, Knowledge (arcana) +16, Listen +15, Move Silently +12, Spellcraft +15, Spot +15. Alertness, Exotic Weapon Proficiency, Flyby Attack, Multiattack.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +10 melee for 1d4, or +3 scourge of idiocy +11 melee for 1d4 + 3 and Intelligence damage.
Full attack. Two claws +10 melee for 1d4 each, or the same scourge strike.
Scourge of idiocy. A strike deals 1d3 Intelligence damage unless the target succeeds on a DC 15 Will save.
See Fury shared rules for Rake and Breath Weapon.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Casts as a 10th-level sorcerer. Save DC 12 + spell level. Printed spells per day by level 0–5: 6/7/7/6/5/3.
0: daze, dancing lights, detect magic, detect poison, disrupt undead, flare, light, ray of frost, resistance.
1st: cause fear, chill touch, color spray, hold portal, magic missile.
2nd: darkness, flaming sphere, protection from arrows, web.
3rd: dispel magic, lightning bolt, stinking cloud.
4th: lesser globe of invulnerability. The book also lists polymorph any object here.
5th: cone of cold.

gm.title: Fury shared rules
lines:
Printed source. Furies, pp. 79–80. The sisters appear together and speak all humanoid languages. They try three times to divert a target from atonement before trying to kill them in public.
Defenses. Damage reduction 15/good. Immune to paralysis, polymorph, and mind-affecting effects.
Scourge. The +3 scourge works like a whip that deals 1d4 lethal damage before modifiers. A Fury may substitute it for her claw attacks. Use the attack and ability damage listed for that sister. Rake (Ex) is +9 melee for 1d4 + 1 damage.
Alter Self (Sp). At will as a standard action, a Fury can take the form of an elderly human woman indefinitely. Caster level 10.
Breath Weapon (Su, 3/day). Fill one adjacent square with foul air. Apply stinking cloud as cast by an 8th-level sorcerer, with a DC 16 Fortitude save.
Find Penitent (Su). Furies can locate a target who seeks redemption at the invitation or embrace stage of corruption. The target cannot hide from them, even with magic.
Gaseous Death (Su). At 0 HP, a Fury and her scourge dissolve into smoke. Surviving sisters continue to fight, though the last survivor tries to flee. If a sister survives, the slain Furies return at full HP after 24 hours. To kill them permanently, all three must die within the same 24 hours and an Innocent must deal the killing blows. Their scourges remain after permanent death.
Weaknesses. A good cleric or a paladin can turn each Fury separately by invoking her true name. A turning attempt cannot destroy, rebuke, or command her. A Fury cannot deliberately harm a good creature except with her breath weapon.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The book spells her name Megarea. The single Attack line appears to print 1d4 + 5 scourge damage, while the Full Attack line gives 1d4 + 3. Use 1d4 + 3 in both. Her weapon line calls its effect Intelligence drain, while the combat prose gives Intelligence damage. Use the latter. The listed +3 base attack and +3 grapple are preserved despite her 10 outsider HD.

The book lists polymorph any object as a 4th-level spell, but in 3.5 it is an 8th-level sorcerer spell. Omit it unless the table deliberately adopts the printed exception. The school restriction in the prose also conflicts with the printed spells known.

gm.title: Hit point rule
lines: 7 + 7 × the caregiver’s level in hit points, with one d8 Hit Die per caregiver level.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: An amorphous companion that can wrap itself around its caregiver in the guise of clothing, such as a folded traveling cloak.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor 13 + PB. Dexterity save +1 + PB. Stealth +1 + PB. Acid damage immunity. Immune to Prone. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11.

gm.title: Caregiver scaling
lines: PB is the caregiver’s proficiency bonus.

gm.title: Traits
lines: False Appearance (object form). A motionless mimic passes for an ordinary object.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Shapechanger. As an action, the mimic can become a Small, Medium, or Large object or return to its amorphous form. Only its size changes. Its gear stays unchanged. It returns to its true form if it dies.
Signature Attack (Bite). Melee weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1d6 + PB piercing damage.

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Distracting Attack (2 Ferocity). Make a signature attack. On a hit, the next attack against the target before the start of the mimic’s next turn has advantage.
Level 3, Adhesive Pseudopods (5 Ferocity). Choose any creatures within 5 ft. Each makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB or is Grappled (escape DC 10 + PB).
Level 5, I’m You (8 Ferocity). Use Shapechanger to copy one Large or smaller creature the mimic sees within 5 ft. Only size changes, and the mimic reverts to its previous form at the start of its next turn. After transforming it can make a signature attack against the creature it copied. Hit or miss, the creature then makes a Wisdom save against DC 10 + PB. On a failure, until the start of the mimic’s next turn it has disadvantage on attacks and saves, and attacks against it have advantage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines:
Wearable Companion. Within 5 ft. of its caregiver, the mimic can enter the caregiver’s space, cover them, and take the form of clothing. Its space is not difficult terrain for the caregiver, who gains advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. While neither is Incapacitated, the caregiver can change the clothing’s appearance at will without an action.
An attack that hits either the caregiver or the worn mimic hits both, and both take the full damage and effects. While worn, the mimic cannot move and can only use a bonus action to revert to its previous form. It also reverts automatically if it enters a rampage. On reverting, it stops being worn and enters the nearest unoccupied space of its choice.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A small amorphous shapechanger that can masquerade as a palm-sized lockbox, with tiny teeth and sticky pseudopods.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 10. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
In Your Space. The mimiature and another creature can occupy the same space. It can pass through openings at least 1 inch wide without squeezing.
Minion. Damage from an attack or failed save reduces the mimiature to 0 HP. Other damage kills it if it reaches 8 damage. It ignores smaller amounts from those other effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Sticky Swarm (Group Attack). Melee weapon attack +3, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1 bludgeoning damage. Through the end of its next turn, the target has disadvantage on checks and saves to escape the Grappled condition and advantage on checks to initiate or maintain a grapple. If at least three mimiatures join the attack, for the same duration the target cannot cast spells with somatic components, drop objects, or interact with objects it is not already holding.
Group Shapechanger. A mimiature can turn into a Tiny object or return to its amorphous form. Four mimiatures within 5 ft. of one another can use this action together to become one Small object. Gear stays unchanged. The combined form breaks if any member moves, takes an action, or dies, returning its members to their true forms.

gm.title: Minion rules
lines:
Group attack. Two to five mimiatures on the same turn can each spend an action to attack one target within reach of all of them. Roll once at +3 plus the number joining. A hit deals 1 bludgeoning damage per mimiature. A lone mimiature uses +3. Advantage or disadvantage applies only if all participants have it. Roll for separate groups if cover or concealment differs. The target chooses a single participant for responses that only affect one attacker.
Group opportunity attack. If a creature provokes from multiple mimiatures at the same time, each can spend its reaction to join. Mimiatures have no Hit Dice and cannot score critical hits.
Overkill. If a weapon hit deals more than 8 damage, apply the surplus to other eligible mimiatures, dropping one to 0 HP for each 8 surplus damage or fraction of 8. In melee, they must be within the weapon’s reach. At range, they must be on the line through the original target within the weapon’s short range. Opportunity attacks cannot deal overkill damage.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Goring Horns (group attack). Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 3 piercing damage. If at least two lackeys joined the attack, the target makes a Strength save with DC 10 plus the number of participants. On a failure, move the target horizontally 5 ft. per participating lackey.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions with the same stat block can share a turn. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice.
Group attacks. Two to five minions sharing a turn can spend their actions on a single attack against a target in every participant’s range or reach. Add +1 to the roll per participant. On a hit, multiply the listed damage by the number of participants. Only use advantage or disadvantage when it applies to everyone involved. Split groups if the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion attacking alone uses its printed bonus and damage. Eligible minions can each spend a reaction to join the same group opportunity attack. If a reaction or similar effect from the target would affect one attacker, the target chooses which participant it affects.
Overkill. A weapon attack that deals more damage than the minion’s maximum HP can apply the excess to another minion with the same block. Keep subtracting each extra target’s HP from the excess to find what carries over. Extra melee targets must be in reach. Extra ranged targets must be on the attack’s line and within the weapon’s short range. An opportunity attack cannot overkill.

lines: Solitary, always neutral evil, no treasure. May appear in any environment.

gm.title: Dread elemental rules
lines:
Printed source. Elemental, Dread, p. 63, and Mists subtype, pp. 7–8.
In Ravenloft, calling a standard elemental has a 20% chance of producing a dread elemental. Summoning magic always produces the dread form. Accidental dread elementals are uncontrolled, and the Dark Powers supply the matching materials. Intentional conjuring requires the matching material and uses the usual chance for the elemental to break control.
Dread elementals understand speech but do not communicate. Their Mists subtype makes them native throughout Ravenloft and allows them to be summoned in any domain. A dismissed dread elemental returns to Ravenloft itself, so the realm's restrictions on calling do not break the calling pact.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Infuse Evil prints the Will DC without a base 10. Using its printed formula, the tier DCs are 1, 3, 6, 11, 14, and 17. Its printed Fortitude DC stays 15.

gm.title: Description
lines: This skeletal ferryman herds travelers deeper into the Mists. If subdued, it may trade passage for its freedom.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Misty border and fogbanks on any land. Solitary. Always neutral evil. No treasure. Advancement 6–9 HD (Large). No level adjustment listed. Can communicate with any creature that has a language.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +7. AC +3 Dex and +4 natural, touch 13, flat-footed 14. Base attack +2, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +1, Ref +4, Will +6.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Undead traits, +2 turn resistance, damage reduction 5/magic. Obscuring Mist (Su). When summoned within a domain, obscuring mist at caster level 12th remains centered on it. It vanishes if that mist is dispelled. Mist does not obscure the ferryman’s own vision.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +4 melee (1d6 + 2 plus ferryman’s rot). Full attack. Two claws +4 each and bite −1 melee (1d8 + 1); each hit can transmit rot.
Ferryman’s Rot (Su). Injury disease. DC 15 Fortitude, incubation 1 week, initial damage 1d4 Con. It persists until remove disease or similar magic cures it, or the victim reaches Constitution 0 and dies. An afflicted victim who dies rises as a mist ferryman after 6 rounds and retreats into the Mists.
Summoning Howl (Ex). When outmatched, call 1d8 + 1 other ferrymen. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and help until combat ends.

gm.title: Summoned ferryman
lines: Someone can conjure it with summon monster VII, but it attacks the summoner. If incapacitated, it can bargain for release by taking itself and all adjacent creatures to a requested spot in Ravenloft, as with greater teleport.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The special-attack summary says mist poison, while the attacks and detailed rules use ferryman’s rot. Ongoing damage is not listed separately. Use the 3.5 disease timing and the printed 1d4 Constitution damage on a failed daily save as a table default, while preserving the exception to natural recovery.

gm.title: Description
lines: A construct forms out of the Mists, wearing the face of the person whose attempt to create it went wrong.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +8. AC −1 size, +2 Dex, +9 natural. Touch AC 11, flat-footed AC 18. Base attack +13, grapple +21. Space 10 ft., reach 10 ft. Fort +11, Ref +8, Will +11.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +21 melee for 3d6 + 8. Full attack makes two slams at the same bonus and damage.
Infuse Essence (Su). A critical hit that kills the target turns it into a mist horror. Finding and capturing that creature is required before restoring the victim to life. A target that survives becomes ethereal and unable to act for 10 rounds. Damage directed at the golem goes to that victim instead. Direct physical attacks against the victim require a magic weapon. If the victim dies during the effect, it becomes a mist horror.
Mist Door (Su). The golem spends the round doing nothing else, and attacks against it gain +2. It retreats into the Mists the following round, leaving thick fog that clears after an hour.
Mournful Howl (Su). Anyone within 50 ft. must make a DC 15 Will save or flee in terror. The howl is audible up to a mile away.
Ram (Ex). Its blows against structures work like a battering ram.
Spellshroud (Sp). The mist extends 15 ft. beyond the golem and produces one of ten spells per use, each usable once per day. When surprised, it releases a random unused effect. Use each spell's usual save type with a −4 penalty to its DC. Roll 1d10 if needed: 1 cloudkill, 2 confusion, 3 blindness, 4 hold person, 5 Tasha's hideous laughter, 6 Otto's irresistible dance, 7 stinking cloud, 8 silence, 9 vampiric touch, 10 slow.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Damage reduction 10/magic. Mists subtype. The Demiplane of Dread is its home plane. In foggy conditions its targets take −2 initiative.
Magic Immunity (Ex). Immune to spells, spell-like abilities and supernatural effects. Damage-dealing spells heal 1 HP per 2 damage they would normally deal if the golem is injured. Dispel magic has no effect.
Construct traits. Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, disease and similar effects. Critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability damage, energy drain and death from massive damage do not affect it, subject to the exceptions below.

gm.title: Dread golem commands
lines: The creator can give commands from within 60 ft. if the golem can see and hear them. It follows the last command and responds to attacks against it. Some dread golems act independently.

gm.title: Specific Focus (Ex)
lines: At creation, its focus was exposed to moonlight within 50 ft. of both golem and creator. The object weighs at most 5 lb. and is worth at least 10,000 gp. A holder can command five tasks. The golem cannot harm the holder while they carry the item. It follows instructions literally and increasingly twists their intent. After the fifth task, the focus vanishes and appears elsewhere in Ravenloft. The golem then hunts its former holder.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Climb +11, Hide +6, Jump +12, Listen +4, Move Silently +6, Spot +4, Survival +4. Alertness, Blind-Fight, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Power Attack.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any terrain in the Mists. Solitary, always chaotic evil, no treasure. Advances to 19–23 HD (Huge) or 24–30 HD (Gargantuan).

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The prose gives no duration for the howl’s flight and no caster level or base save DC for Spellshroud. The header labels +13/+21 as Base Attack. Use the second value as grapple, following the adjacent stat blocks.

gm.title: Description
lines: A ripple stalks travelers in the Mists. It gathers into a shape, sometimes borrowing the thing its victim fears most.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Printed common example based on a 5th-level human rogue. Ravenloft Mists, solitary, neutral evil, no treasure. Advancement 6–9 HD (Medium), 10–14 HD (Large).

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC 13 (+1 Dex, +2 natural). Base attack +2, grapple +5 as printed. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +1, Ref +5, Will +2. Climb +8, Disable Device +7, Hide +14, Listen +10, Move Silently +13, Open Locks +10, Spot +14. Alertness, Balance, Blind-Fight, Improved Initiative, Stealthy.

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 10/magic, incorporeal and undead traits, and +5 turn resistance in the sample. Immune to holy water, charm, spells that normally affect undead, and spells that need a physical body, such as blindness/deafness. SR 10 applies to spells cast within 20 ft. and leaves spell-like abilities and spell-producing magic items unaffected.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +5 melee (2d6 + 3). Full attack: two slams at +5, each for 2d6 + 3. The published sample lists sneak attack 3d6 + 3.
Assemble. It takes 1d4 turns to form a body capable of attacking. Until formed, creatures in the Mists can detect the hint of its presence with DC 20 Spot. The horror can break off combat by dispersing and must then spend another 1d4 turns reassembling.
Telempathic Projection (Sp). Send emotions or short messages to anyone within 120 ft. who is in the Mists. DC 15 Will lets a recipient resist or ignore it. A common horror stays in one area and may send false reassurance to make travelers pause while it assembles.

gm.title: Wandering mist horror
lines: Uses the common horror’s statistics, can roam the Mists and actively seeks prey. Fear Aura (Su), once daily: everyone within 120 ft. makes a DC 15 Fear check. It uses the aura early, in the first normal combat round if it surprised the targets. Suggestion (Sp), once daily: one creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 15 Will save to resist a telepathic suggestion.

gm.title: Creating a Mist Horror
lines: Apply to a living creature. Keep size, base attack, saves, and skill points, and change type to undead with the original type augmented. All present and future Hit Dice become d12. Give fly 30 ft. or retain a faster base fly speed. Keep base natural armor and add deflection equal to the higher of +1 or its Cha modifier. Replace ordinary attacks with natural attacks and keep the base special attacks and qualities. Add DR 10/magic, the immunities, SR 10, projection, and +4 turn resistance. Remove Con, add +2 Cha, and give +4 racial bonuses to Hide, Move Silently, and Spot. Keep skills usable in incorporeal form and add Improved Initiative and Stealthy. CR is base +1. Any evil, solitary, no treasure, no level adjustment, and the sample’s advancement ranges.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The encounter sample retains Con 15, natural armor without a deflection bonus, and +5 turn resistance. The template removes Con, adds deflection, and grants +4 turn resistance. Use the displayed numbers for the printed sample.

The projection rule specifies a DC 15 Will save. The common horror’s tactics instead mention an opposed Will check when it offers false reassurance. Use the listed DC for a quick ruling. The template prints 'average good' maneuverability. Use good, as in the encounter sample.

gm.title: Lycanthrope encounter rules
lines:
Printed source. Lycanthrope, pp. 137 and 148.
Alternate Form (Su). Where available, take or leave an animal or hybrid form as a standard action. Equipment does not change. Entering either form heals as a day of rest. A slain lycanthrope returns to humanoid form where it has one, but severed parts keep their animal shape. An afflicted creature normally gains one alternate form and can struggle to control it.
Curse of Lycanthropy (Su). A qualifying bite to a humanoid within one size category requires Fortitude DC 18 or transmits the curse. Bludgeoning or nonpenetrating attacks cannot transmit it. Afflicted lycanthropes can spread it in Ravenloft. The general text specifies animal form, but a listed hybrid curse also uses this procedure at the table. Use any strain-specific exception below.
Natural lycanthropes generally have DR 10/silver in animal or hybrid form, while afflicted ones have DR 5/silver. Some strains name a different material. Low-light vision and scent work in any form unless the profile specifies otherwise. Lycanthropic empathy allows simple communication, gives a +4 racial bonus on attitude checks with the corresponding normal or dire animal, and permits simple commands to friendly animals.
A spellcaster cannot use verbal, somatic, or material components in animal form and cannot use verbal components in hybrid form. Apply the printed encounter stats for each form.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Innate Spellcasting. The hag’s innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). She can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components: At will: detect magic, magic missile 2/day each: plane shift (self only), ray of enfeeblement, sleep Magic Resistance. The hag has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Claws (Hag Form Only). Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage. Change Shape. The hag magically polymorphs into a Small or Medium female humanoid, or back into her true form. Her statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment she is wearing or carrying isn’t transformed. She reverts to her true form if she dies. Etherealness. The hag magically enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. To do so, the hag must have a heartstone in her possession. Nightmare Haunting (1/Day). While on the Ethereal Plane, the hag magically touches a sleeping humanoid on the Material Plane. A protection from evil and good spell cast on the target prevents this contact, as does a magic circle. As long as the contact persists, the target has dreadful visions. If these visions last for at least 1 hour, the target gains no benefit from its rest, and its hit point maximum is reduced by 5 (1d10). If this effect reduces the target’s hit point maximum to 0, the target dies, and if the target was evil, its soul is trapped in the hag’s soul bag. The reduction to the target’s hit point maximum lasts until removed by the greater restoration spell or similar magic.

lines: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 176, 178–179. The coven sidebar is on p. 176. The official errata corrects innate spellcasting, Claws, and resistance wording.

gm.title: Variant rules
lines: Night Hag (Coven) is the other library label for this printed coven profile.

gm.title: Shared spellcasting
lines:
A coven has three hags of any type. All three can use these wizard spells while they are within 30 ft. of one another. Track one pool of spell slots for the whole coven. Each hag casts as a 12th-level spellcaster using Intelligence. This hag uses spell save DC 15 and +7 to hit with spell attacks for this list.
1st level (4 slots): Identify, Ray of Sickness.
2nd level (3 slots): Hold Person, Locate Object.
3rd level (3 slots): Bestow Curse, Counterspell, Lightning Bolt.
4th level (3 slots): Phantasmal Killer, Polymorph.
5th level (2 slots): Contact Other Plane, Scrying.
6th level (1 slot): Eyebite.

gm.title: Hag Eye
lines: A coven can have one Hag Eye. A coven member on the same plane can spend an action to see through it. The eye has AC 10, 1 HP, and darkvision 60 ft. If it is destroyed, each coven member takes 3d10 psychic damage and becomes Blinded for 24 hours. All three hags must perform a 1-hour ritual to make a new eye. They cannot do so while Blinded, and an action outside the ritual makes them start over.

gm.title: Hag Coven
lines: When all three coven members are within 30 ft. of one another, each casts with Intelligence as a 12th-level caster. The coven shares the spell slots. Each hag has save DC 12 plus her Intelligence modifier and spell attack bonus 4 plus that modifier.

Slots and spells by tier: 1st (4) identify, ray of sickness. 2nd (3) hold person, locate object. 3rd (3) bestow curse, counterspell, lightning bolt. 4th (3) phantasmal killer, polymorph. 5th (2) contact other plane, scrying. 6th (1) eyebite.

The three can create one hag eye in an uninterrupted hour. A hag can spend an action to see through it from the same plane. It has AC 10, 1 HP and Darkvision 60 ft. Destroying it deals 3d10 psychic damage to each member and Blinds them for 24 hours.

gm.title: Description
lines: A manscorpion wears a grimacing mask and protective makeup above ground. Without that protection, the curse of Idu makes sunlight deadly.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Rare in tropical and subtropical deserts or caves. Squad or city, usually 8 or more. Carnivore. Intelligence 5–18. Morale 15–18. Treasure J, K, M, Q, with F and U × 10 listed parenthetically. No magic resistance. 60-foot infravision. Stands 6 feet tall, with a 4-foot body and 10-foot tail.

gm.title: Hit Dice, THAC0 and XP
lines:
6 HD: THAC0 15, 975 XP (1,400 with a Legacy).
7 HD: THAC0 13, 1,400 XP (2,000 with a Legacy).
8 HD: THAC0 13, 2,000 XP (3,000 with a Legacy).
9–10 HD: THAC0 11.
11–12 HD: THAC0 9.
Add 1,000 XP for each HD above 8.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws and sting. Two front-facing claws deal 1d4 + 1 apiece. The tail can strike to any side and deals 1d4 plus poison on a hit. The stat line also allows weapon damage without specifying a weapon routine.
Sting poison. At 6–8 HD, a failed save vs. poison puts the victim to sleep for 2d8 rounds. At 9–10 HD it deals 3d8 damage on failure. At 11–12 HD, save vs. poison at −2 or die immediately.

gm.title: Sunlight and armor
lines:
Armor rated AC 7 or worse improves its AC by only 1. It cannot swim, and water washes off its makeup in 1d4 rounds.
Direct sun with no makeup deals 1d6 + 2 damage per round until the creature gets underground or reapplies all makeup. gm.title: Description
lines: A nosferatu can return from apparent death in direct moonlight. By day, it relies on servants already under its control.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Fledgling sample, 5th-level human aristocrat. Initiative +8. Touch AC 14, flat-footed AC 22. BAB +3, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +6.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Choose slam +4 melee (1d6 + 1), +1 rapier +8 melee (1d6 + 2, 18–20), or masterwork heavy crossbow +8 ranged (1d10, 19–20/×2).
Domination (Su). Standard action on a target within 30 ft. that the vampire can look at. Will DC 18 or dominate person at caster level 12.
Blood Drain (Ex). Pin a living target in a grapple. Each round the pin holds, drain 1d4 Constitution and gain 5 temporary HP. Each victim of Blood Drain must also make a DC 18 Will save or be dominated until break enchantment succeeds or the vampire dies.
Children of the Night (Su, 1/day). Standard action to call 1d6 + 1 rat swarms, 1d4 + 1 bat swarms, or 3d6 wolves. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 10/silver and magic, cold and electricity resistance 10, turn resistance +4, spider climb, undead traits. Gaseous form as a standard action at will, with indefinite duration and fly speed 20 ft. (perfect). Alternate Form can assume bat, dire bat, wolf, or dire wolf form. As a standard action assume the listed animal form. Lose the slam and domination, gain the animal’s natural weapons and extraordinary attacks, and retain this form until the next sunrise or another change.
Lunar Regeneration. Direct moonlight converts past damage to nonlethal damage even after apparent death. Heal 3, 4, 6, or 8 per round in crescent, half, gibbous, or full moonlight, plus the age bonus. Fire, acid, and blessed or holy weapons deal normal damage. It can reattach severed limbs. It cannot regenerate a lost limb or recover nonlethal damage with its head detached.
Restful Sleep. While at 1 HP or more, heal 1 HP per HD per hour in its coffin. Daylight disables supernatural abilities. After exposure to direct sunlight, it must sleep in its coffin for 8 hours to restore them. Existing domination persists, and an alternate form cannot end until powers return.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: A humanoid or monstrous humanoid drained to Constitution 0 or less rises on the next full moon. At 4 HD or fewer it becomes spawn, otherwise a nosferatu. Spawn remain controlled until the creator dies. Nosferatu spawn retain charm, gaseous form, spider climb and daylight powerlessness. They heal 2 HP per hour asleep in their coffins if at 1 HP or more, or 2 HP per round in direct full moonlight.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines: Garlic repels it, and a clearly presented holy symbol or mirror keeps it 5 ft. away. It cannot enter a private home without invitation. A stake through the heart kills it while left in place. At 0 HP it collapses but may return in moonlight. Burn the whole body or scatter the severed limbs beyond its minions’ reach. Running water costs one-third of HP each round and destroys it after 3 rounds of immersion.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +21, Diplomacy +16, Gather Information +11, Hide +12, Intimidate +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +12, Search +13, Sense Motive +15, Spot +12. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Diplomacy), Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Encounter adaptation
lines: Apply the strain to the 3.5 vampire template. Retain unmodified abilities, size, BAB, saves and skill points. The base vampire uses undead d12 Hit Dice and has no Constitution score. Keep an existing swim speed and ignore vulnerability to immersion in running water if the base creature can swim. Use save DC 10 + half HD rounded down + Charisma modifier unless specified. Age rows replace one another. Nosferatu lack the base vampire’s Energy Drain. Age DR always requires silver and magic. The cerebral subtype changes the feeding attack only.

gm.title: Description
lines: This blood-drinking undead keeps the skills and spells of its former life. It can pass for a living person in daylight, though it casts no shadow and has no reflection.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any terrain. Very rare, solitary, and active at any time. Drinks blood. Intelligence 8–18. Treasure F. Any alignment, usually evil. Appearing 1. No magic resistance. Height 5–7 feet. Morale 15–16. The XP listed is the minimum.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite or weapon. One bite deals 1d4 damage. It can instead use a weapon or cast a spell from its former class. Use the THAC0 of the equivalent class and level. Strength is at least 16.
Charm. A creature that meets its gaze saves at −2 or is affected as by charm person. The nosferatu can then use suggestion on that victim.
Change form. It can become gaseous at will and is immune to physical attacks in that form. At night it can become a large bat. By day it can become a raven. It can also use spider climb.
Summon animals. Call 1d100 rats or bats underground, or 3d6 wolves in the wilderness. They arrive in 2d6 rounds.

gm.title: Defenses and defeat
lines:
Only +1 or better magical weapons can harm it. It regains 1 HP each round. Sleep, charm, hold, poison, and paralysis fail against it. Cold and electricity spells deal half damage. At 0 HP it turns gaseous and flees to its coffin. If it fails to reach the coffin within 12 turns, it dies. After eight hours inside, it regains corporeal form.
Garlic repels it. Clerical symbols and holy water are harmless to it. A cleric of opposing alignment or a cleric specialized in hunting undead can turn it. Immersion in running water for three consecutive rounds destroys it. A wooden stake through the heart stops it, but it resumes healing if the stake is removed. To destroy a staked nosferatu permanently, behead it and fill its mouth with earth consecrated to a good deity.

gm.title: Invitation and spawn
lines: A resident must invite it into a private home. Charm or deception can secure the invitation. Once invited, it can come and go. If it chooses to create spawn, a drained human or humanoid rises after three days unless the body is burned or destroyed. The spawn obeys its creator until the creator dies.

gm.title: Former class
lines: Keep the original class’s memories, abilities, skills, and restrictions. Set class level to at least 7 and at most 9 when it becomes a nosferatu. It can advance thereafter at triple the usual XP. Keep ability scores except that Strength is at least 16 and Constitution is no longer required. Warriors and clerics can wear armor without improving AC. Clerics retain spells from their original Immortal patron only if their alignment still matches.

gm.title: Hunger and Red Curse
lines: It must drink at least 9 HP worth of mortal blood per week. After a week of fasting, its ability scores fall by 1 each day to a minimum of 9. An extra 1d4 HP worth of fresh blood restores lost scores. Nonhumanoid blood dulls the pain for one day without restoring scores. It never acquires Legacies and needs no cinnabryl.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Demon Prince of Undeath rules Thanatos from the fortress city of Naratyr. He wants to extinguish all life and rule the Undead that remain.

gm.title: Armor
lines: Natural armor. AC 20 while holding the Wand of Orcus.

gm.title: Damage immunities
lines: Necrotic and poison. Nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When Orcus fails a save, he can spend a use to succeed.
Magic Resistance. Orcus has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Master of Undeath. Orcus can cast Animate Dead at will and Create Undead three times per day. He chooses the level for each casting. The resulting Undead obey him indefinitely. He can cast Create Undead at any time of day.
Special Equipment. Orcus carries the Wand of Orcus.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Wand of Orcus, Tail, or Necrotic Bolt.
Wand of Orcus. Melee weapon attack, +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 24 (3d8 + 11) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (2d12) necrotic damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) force damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.
Necrotic Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +15 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 29 (5d8 + 7) necrotic damage.
Conjure Undead (1/day). While holding the Wand of Orcus, summon any combination of Undead with a total of up to 500 average hit points. They appear in unoccupied spaces within 300 ft. and obey Orcus until destroyed or dismissed by him as an action.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast a listed spell using Charisma (save DC 23). No material components are required.
At will. Detect Magic.
3/day. Dispel Magic.
1/day. Time Stop.
Wand Spellcasting. While holding the Wand of Orcus, use an action to cast a listed spell (save DC 18). The wand holds up to 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 charges each dawn.
At will from the wand. Animate Dead, Blight, Speak with Dead.
1 charge each. Circle of Death or Finger of Death.
2 charges. Power Word Kill.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Orcus has 3 legendary actions and regains them at the start of his turn. Spend the stated cost on one option immediately after another creature's turn. He cannot use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, he must finish his first turn before using one.
Attack (1 action). Make one Tail or Necrotic Bolt attack.
Creeping Death (2 actions). Choose a point on the ground that Orcus can see within 100 ft. A cylinder 60 ft. high and 10 ft. in radius rises from that point until the end of his next turn. Creatures inside have vulnerability to necrotic damage.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
At initiative count 20, after any creature tied at that count, Orcus can use one option while in his lair and able to act. He cannot repeat the same option two rounds in a row. If surprised, he must finish his first turn before using one.
Deadly Utterance. Subject one creature Orcus knows is in his lair to Power Word Kill. He can target a creature he cannot see.
Grasp of the Dead. Conjure skeletal arms in a visible 20-ft. square of ground until the next initiative count 20. Each creature in the square when the arms appear makes a DC 23 Strength save. On a failure, it is restrained until the arms vanish or Orcus releases it, which requires no action.
Undead Servants. Animate up to six corpses in the lair as skeletons, zombies, or ghouls. They obey Orcus's telepathic commands anywhere in the lair.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
One or both effects can occur in the region around the lair.
Charnel Realm. The region smells of rotting flesh and fills with swarms of flies.
Undead Beasts. Some dead Beasts rise as skeletons or zombies. Undead versions of local wildlife are common.
These effects fade over 1d10 days after Orcus dies.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Demon Prince of Undeath rules from Naratyr, a fortress city on Thanatos. He rewards cultists who raise the dead and keeps an undead army under his command.

gm.title: Armor
lines: Natural armor. AC 20 while holding the Wand of Orcus.

gm.title: Damage immunities
lines: Necrotic, poison. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical sources.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Wand of Orcus. The wand holds up to 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 at dawn. Its abilities that call for a save use DC 18. While holding it, Orcus can use an action to cast Animate Dead, Blight, or Speak with Dead. He can also cast Circle of Death or Finger of Death for 1 charge each, or Power Word Kill for 2 charges.
Legendary Resistance (3/day). If Orcus fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed.
Magic Resistance. Orcus has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. Orcus’s weapon attacks are magical.
Master of Undeath. Orcus chooses the spell level when he casts Animate Dead or Create Undead. The creatures they create remain under his control indefinitely. He can cast Create Undead at any time of day.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
Orcus uses Charisma (spell save DC 23, +15 to hit with spell attacks). He needs no material components.
At will. Chill Touch (17th level), Detect Magic.
3/day each. Create Undead, Dispel Magic.
1/day. Time Stop.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Wand of Orcus attacks.
Wand of Orcus. Melee weapon attack, +19 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (2d12) necrotic damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) piercing damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.
Conjure Undead (Wand of Orcus, once per dawn). While holding the wand, Orcus creates undead creatures with no more than 500 combined average hit points. They appear in unoccupied spaces within 300 ft. and obey him until destroyed or dismissed. Dismissing them takes an action.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Orcus has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of his turn. He can use one option at the end of another creature’s turn.
Tail (1 action). Make one Tail attack.
A Taste of Undeath (1 action). Cast Chill Touch at 17th level.
Creeping Death (2 actions). Choose a point on the ground Orcus can see within 100 ft. A cylinder 60 ft. high with a 10-ft. radius appears there until the end of Orcus’s next turn. Creatures inside have vulnerability to necrotic damage.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, losing initiative ties, Orcus can use one option. He cannot pick the same option two rounds in a row.
Power Word Kill. One creature Orcus knows is in the lair is subject to Power Word Kill. He can choose it without seeing it. The spell uses its normal hit-point threshold.
Animate Corpses. Raise up to six corpses in the lair as skeletons, zombies, or ghouls. They obey Orcus by telepathy from anywhere in the lair.
Skeletal Arms. Choose a 20-ft. square on the ground Orcus can see. Each creature in the square when the arms appear must succeed on a DC 23 Strength save or be restrained. The arms vanish at the next initiative count 20. Orcus can release their grasp before then without taking an action.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Dead beasts sometimes animate, and skeletal or zombified local wildlife roam the area.
The air reeks of decay and swarms with flies, even without carrion.
A humanoid who spends at least 1 hour within 1 mile of the lair must make a DC 23 Wisdom save. On a failure, roll on the Madness of Orcus table. A success grants immunity to this regional effect for 24 hours.
After Orcus dies, these effects fade over 1d10 days.

gm.title: Madness of Orcus
lines:
Roll d100 when a creature succumbs to this madness in the lair or within Orcus’s sight. The resulting flaw lasts until cured.
01–20. Withdraws into bitter thoughts about living.
21–40. Feels driven to torment the weak.
41–60. Disturbs the dead freely while trying to understand death.
61–80. Seeks to become undead and endure forever.
81–100. Dwells on the futility of life.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The adventure gives Oscar a fixed 72 HP and supplies no replacement Hit Dice. The profile retains the base Hit Dice for effects that count them.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A broad, tawny owlbear with a feathered face, hooked beak and curved talons.

gm.title: Caregiver scaling
lines: PB is the caregiver’s proficiency bonus.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Keen Sight and Smell. The owlbear has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight or smell.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Signature Attack (Claw). Melee weapon attack at +3 + PB, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1d6 + PB slashing damage.

gm.title: Ferocity actions
lines:
Level 1, Violent Attack (2 Ferocity). Make a signature attack. A hit deals extra damage equal to PB and lets the owlbear move the target 5 ft. in any direction.
Level 3, Owlie Oop (5 Ferocity). Leap up to half speed without provoking opportunity attacks. On landing, every creature within 5 ft. of the owlbear makes a Strength save against DC 10 + PB or falls Prone.
Level 5, Bear Hug (8 Ferocity). Choose a visible creature within 5 ft. It makes a Dexterity save against DC 10 + PB. A failure deals PBd10 bludgeoning damage and leaves it Grappled, with escape DC 10 + PB. On success it takes half damage. While grappled this way it is Restrained. Using Bear Hug or the signature attack against a different target ends the grapple.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Give a Hoot (long rest). The owlbear hoots. If its caregiver hears it, the caregiver gains 5 × PB temporary hit points.

gm.title: MCDM companion rules
lines:
Shared turn. The caregiver and companion act on the same turn. The companion moves and uses its reaction and bonus action independently. To do anything with its action besides Dash, Disengage or Dodge, it normally needs a command that costs the caregiver a bonus action. It must see or hear the caregiver. If the caregiver is Incapacitated, it can act without a command. The GM chooses who controls it when the caregiver is Incapacitated or absent.
Ferocity. At the start of their turn, unless Incapacitated, the companion gains 1d4 Ferocity plus one for each enemy it sees or hears within 5 ft. A swarm sharing one stat block counts as one enemy. Spend the listed cost before taking a Ferocity action. It uses the companion’s action, requires the listed caregiver level and is unavailable during a rampage.
Rampage. After rolling Ferocity, a companion with at least 10 Ferocity risks a rampage if it is not Incapacitated. A caregiver who is not Incapacitated and can be seen or heard can prevent it with a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check against DC 5 + Ferocity, without spending an action. If the companion rampages, it immediately moves toward the nearest creature it senses and makes its signature attack, with extra damage equal to half its Ferocity on a hit. If an ally and enemy tie for nearest, roll any die. On an odd roll the caregiver’s player chooses a tied ally. On an even roll they choose a tied enemy. If it cannot reach a target, it Dashes toward it. If it senses none, it moves as far as it can in a random safe direction. Ferocity falls to 0 after this action or at the end of the turn.
Recovery. At 0 HP, a companion makes death saves. After combat, Ferocity resets to 0. A companion that is not dying first regains HP equal to its remaining Ferocity.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
16th-level wizard. Intelligence, save DC 18, +10 to hit.
At will: Chill Touch, Mage Hand, Mending, Prestidigitation, Shocking Grasp.
1st level (4 slots): Delerium Orb, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Shield.
2nd level (3 slots): Hold Person, Invisibility, Warp Bolt.
3rd level (3 slots): Counterspell, Lightning Bolt, Purge Contamination.
4th level (3 slots): Delerium Blast, Forced Evolution.

6th level (1 slot): Chain Lightning.
7th level (1 slot): Octarine Spray.

gm.title: Setting Spells
lines:
Delerium Orb. Action, 120 ft. One visible creature makes a save using an ability chosen by the caster. Choose cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, psychic, or radiant damage. Deal 6d6 on failure or half on success, plus 2d6 per slot level above 1st.
Warp Bolt. Action, 60 ft., concentrate up to 1 minute. Automatically hit a contaminated target, or make a ranged spell attack against an uncontaminated one. A hit deals 6d6 necrotic and one level of Contamination. On later turns, use an action for a new bolt. Each slot level above 2nd permits one more target.
Delerium Blast. Action, 150 ft. Creatures in a 20-ft.-radius sphere make an Intelligence save. Failure deals 10d6 psychic damage and Incapacitates until the end of the target's next turn. Success halves damage and prevents Incapacitated. Add 2d6 per slot level above 4th.
Conjure the Deep Haze. Action, 120 ft., concentrate up to 10 minutes. A 20-ft.-radius sphere spreads around corners and is heavily obscured until it ends or strong wind clears it. First entry on a turn or starting a turn there forces a Constitution save. Failure deals 8d6 necrotic and one level of Contamination. Success halves damage without Contamination. Holding breath does not help.
Octarine Spray. Action, 60-ft. cone. Each creature makes a Constitution save. Roll a d8 for each creature. On rolls of 1–5, deal 20d6 psychic, necrotic, force, radiant, or thunder damage respectively, half on success. On a failed save, 6 compels the target to spend its movement approaching the nearest visible creature and use its action to attack a random creature in reach, with a Wisdom save at each turn's end to stop. A 7 causes a level of Contamination at each turn's start, with a Constitution save at each turn's end to stop. An 8 adds two rolls and can repeat.
Each spell above consumes a 100 gp delerium fragment and gives its caster one level of Contamination.
Purge Contamination. One hour, touch. Consume 100 gp of alchemical fluids or holy water to clear a humanoid's Contamination and mutations. It gains one Exhaustion level per level removed.
Forced Evolution. Eight hours, touch. Consume a 250 gp alchemical mixture to replace one mutation with one selected by the GM or rolled randomly.
Siphon Contamination. One hour, touch. Consume 500 gp of alchemical fluids and a 5,000 gp delerium geode. A second willing humanoid takes all Contamination removed from a first willing humanoid, whose mutations are also removed. A transformed former humanoid can instead return to their original form if the second willing humanoid has at least their transformed CR in levels or CR. The recipient then undergoes Monstrous Transformation. Preventing the transfer makes the spell fail.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Contaminating Touch. Melee spell attack +8, reach 10 ft., one target, 10 (3d6) necrotic. DC 16 Constitution save or one level of Contamination.
Infest the Flesh (recharge 6). Each creature within 30 ft. makes a DC 16 Dexterity save. Failure deals 22 (5d8) necrotic and Restrains the creature. It takes 22 (5d8) necrotic at the start of each of the Pale Man's turns. It repeats the save at the end of its own turns to end the effect.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines:
Three legendary actions per round. Use one option after another creature's turn and recover spent actions at the start of this creature's turn.
Cantrip. Cast a cantrip.
Slither (2 actions). Move up to speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Contaminate (3 actions). Each target Restrained by Infest the Flesh makes a DC 16 Constitution save or gains one level of Contamination.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Appendix A, pp. 212–213. Setting spells, Appendix D, pp. 227–229.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Contaminating Touch and Infest the Flesh use their printed attack bonus and save DC. These differ from the general Spellcasting numbers.
The stat block lists Siphon Contamination among the 5th-level slots, but Appendix D defines it as a 6th-level spell. Table ruling. Use the Appendix D level when casting it.

gm.title: Description
lines: An infestation creates a problem to diagnose or survive, with a cure that can drive an adventure.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Rare, one infestation. Mindless, no treasure or magic resistance. Parasites neither gain Legacies nor become Afflicted.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Use one infestation procedure below. Parasites have no regular attacks. Award 15 XP for surviving a nonfatal infestation or 65 XP for surviving a potentially fatal one.

gm.title: Inheritor lice
lines: Roll d100 for the degree of infestation. Increase the host’s cinnabryl use by the same percentage, doubling it at 100%. Up to three times per day the lice can trigger Displace and move their host 10 feet in a random direction to evade an incoming physical hit. They sometimes do so at random. Cinnabryl ointment removes them. Saragón lyra birds eat them.

gm.title: Powder moth
lines: Use detect invisibility to see the moths. Roll d100 for the percentage of smokepowder spoiled. While the moths remain, anyone moving the keg saves vs. paralysis or sets it off. A full keg deals 10d6+10 damage within 10 feet and half damage out to 20 feet. Scale damage by the unspoiled fraction, then halve it on a successful save vs. breath weapon. Inheritors within 20 feet lose one week of cinnabryl protection per full 8 points of damage suffered.

gm.title: Jibarú pest
lines: Choose a local pest. A moth’s powder makes victims believe they can fly, and the moth can supply medicine for the Fly Affliction. A brown leech drains several HP of blood per week while preventing the Strength Affliction. A green territorial wasp’s sting kills on a failed save vs. poison. Its nest supplies an ointment that cures vermilia.

gm.title: Lupin plague
lines: Infested grapes or wine transmit the plague. The host saves vs. poison at −3 at the end of each day or dies. Medication or magical healing can end it.

gm.title: Cardinal tick
lines: Roll d100 for the starting infestation and use that percentage as the chance a Legacy fails. Participants in melee against an infested carrier acquire a 5% infestation. Each attempted Legacy use increases infestation by 15 percentage points. Nonhumanoids cap at 50%. Other Red Curse effects still apply. Cinnabryl ointment removes the ticks. Scratching them off costs 1 HP per percentage point removed without rare Jibarú medicine. Saragón lyra birds eat them.

gm.title: Vermilia
lines: Physical contact transmits the infection. Living creatures save vs. poison to avoid it. Undead catch it automatically. Damage starts at 1 on day one and doubles each day. Undead can avoid the day’s damage with a save vs. death magic at the end of that day, with a penalty equal to that day’s damage. All victims take an additional −1 on related saves per Legacy. Infection counts as a +2 weapon for damaging undead or magical creatures. Cure disease, heal or a remedy from vulturehound blood or a suitable Jibarú pest ends the infection. Fire cleanses infested remains.

lines: pp. 84–86, with Displace Legacy on p. 7

gm.title: Heraldic servant rules
lines:
Printed source. Heraldic Servant, General, pp. 44–46.
A heraldic servant has an inactive form on its coat of arms and two active forms, one natural and one humanoid. The rightful bearer can summon one servant at any time. It must touch the coat of arms to return to it or transfer to another coat of arms.
Use the same hit points in either active form. Unless the entry gives an exception, use the same Armor Class and magical powers as well. Weapons and movement may depend on form. An active servant automatically defends its bearer unless ordered otherwise. It can only be killed while active.
An active servant and its bearer can share thoughts and senses telepathically within one mile. While linked, the bearer counts as one experience level higher and shares the servant's spell immunities and magic resistance. While the servant is inactive, personally carrying its coat of arms grants the extra level and magic resistance. Check the individual entry for additional benefits.
The servant's death removes all benefits and permanently costs its bearer two levels. The servant can return at the bearer's deathbed if a new generation takes over. Three consecutive unworthy generations lose its service until two consecutive generations prove worthy.
A heraldic servant needs neither food nor sleep and earns no XP. It remains neutral or takes its bearer's alignment. The Red Curse cannot give it Legacies or Affliction.

lines: A tiny verminlike demon with green eyes and wiry tendrils, whose shape resembles local pests.

gm.title: Classification
lines: Tiny Fiend (Demon, Category 1), typically chaotic evil

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Poison damage immunity. Immune to Poisoned. Darkvision 60 ft., Soulsight 10 ft., passive Perception 8. Language Abyssal.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Horrid Stench. An enemy that starts its turn within 10 ft. of at least three pitlings becomes Poisoned until the start of its next turn.
Minion. An attack or failed save that deals damage drops the pitling to 0 HP. Other damage kills it if it deals at least 11 damage. It ignores smaller amounts from such effects.
Soul Feast. When the pitling reduces a creature other than a Construct or Undead to 0 HP, or deals damage to a dying creature, that creature makes a DC 11 Wisdom save. On failure it dies, its soul is consumed and the pitling becomes a Category 2 demon of the GM’s choice with 1 soul. Only Wish can restore the victim to life. If a group attack brought the victim to 0 HP, the GM picks one participating pitling to consume the soul.
Soulsight. The pitling can sense creatures within 10 ft. except Constructs and Undead. This counts as sight for features that require it. Physical objects, total cover, and supernatural effects do not block this sense unless a rule says they do.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Spit (Group Attack). Melee or ranged weapon attack +4, reach 5 ft. or range 15/30 ft., one target. Hit 4 poison damage.

gm.title: Minion rules
lines:
Group attack. Two to five pitlings on the same turn can each use an action to attack a target in reach or range of all of them. A single roll gets +4 plus the number joining. On a hit, deal 4 poison damage per pitling. A lone pitling uses +4. Advantage or disadvantage applies if every participant has it. Split attackers into separate rolls when cover or concealment differs. The target chooses which participant is affected by a response that can affect just one attacker.
Group opportunity attack. If the target provokes from multiple pitlings at once, each can use its reaction to join the melee Spit attack. Pitlings have no Hit Dice and cannot score critical hits.
Overkill. A weapon hit dealing more than 11 damage leaves surplus that can drop another eligible pitling for every 11 points of surplus damage or part thereof. Melee targets must be in reach. Ranged targets must lie on the line from the attacker through the original target within the weapon’s short range. Opportunity attacks cannot deal overkill damage.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The Ruinant is one published Category 2 form a Pitling may take after Soul Feast.

gm.title: Description
lines: This six-legged predator nests where magic is plentiful. Void cultists lure one to a new gateway to attack travelers, knowing its feeding can destabilize the crossing.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Perception 17, Stealth 13. Resistant to force damage, Exhaustion, Frightened, and Prone. Darkvision 60 ft. Language Abyssal.

gm.title: Ability modifiers
lines: Str +4, Dex +0, Con +3, Int -3, Wis +7, Cha -2

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Magic Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Monstrosity Resilience. Resistance to Exhaustion and Frightened.
Sense Magic. Detect and locate magic within 120 ft. A visible creature or object bearing detectable magic appears outlined by a faint aura.
Shimmering Sail. The sail shimmers within 120 ft. of a magic source. A creature starting its turn within 30 ft. that can see the sail makes a DC 15 Charisma save. On failure it is mesmerized until the start of its next turn. While mesmerized, its speed is halved and it has disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks. Unless Surprised, a creature can avert its eyes at the start of its turn to avoid the save. It cannot see the portal eater until the start of its next turn. Looking at it before then triggers the save immediately.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Gore and two Claw attacks, or three Force Bolt attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit 17 (3d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Gore. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 18 (4d6 + 4) piercing damage.
Force Bolt. Ranged spell attack, +7 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit 17 (3d8 + 4) force damage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Consume Magic (recharge 4–6). Choose a visible spellcaster or magic item within 30 ft. Exclude sentient items and artifacts. A spellcaster loses a slot of the highest circle it can cast unless it passes a DC 15 Charisma save. An item loses 2 (1d4) charges or cannot be activated until it recharges or 24 hours pass, whichever comes first. After draining a target, the portal eater gains 5 temporary HP per circle of the slot or per charge lost, with a minimum of 5 temporary HP.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.
